newsitem.title: USA: Model sues New York lottery over advertisement. [Corrected 19:47 gmt]
newsitem.headline: Model sues New York lottery over advertisement. [Corrected 19:47 gmt]

text.p: A large-size model is suing (corrects from "plans to sue") state officials this week over a New York State Lottery advertisement she claims insulted and ridiculed bigger women.
Carolyn Strauss, who is also a fashion consultant to retailers, told Reuters on Monday she found the wording of the advertising campaign offensive.
The ad, which was for the lottery's "Year End Bonus" 1996 promotion, said: "Marry the client's big-boned daughter -- How to get a bonus whether you deserve one or not."
"The ad ... implied that if you win Lotto (the lottery), you won't have to marry a fat woman," she said. "It makes every fat lady feel badly."
A hearing is scheduled in Manhattan State Supreme Court on Wednesday.
The suit, filed in January, seeks $1 million in damages but Strauss said she would settle for a public apology.
"I want them to say they're sorry in the first place and promise they'll never do it again," she said.
Lawyers representing the New York state lottery did not return calls for comment.
Strauss said she also thought the ad was offensive to men "who love large-size women and who are married to large-size women because it makes them not okay."
Most important, she said, was the need to warn other advertisers that this campaign "is not funny, and we're not going to put up with it."
Strauss, in her early 30s, is 5-foot, 7-inches (1.7 metre) tall and weighs 200 pounds (91 kg). She said she had been a size 18 since she was 16-years-old.
Strauss also is an aerobics instructor and author of a book on large-size modeling.
